Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 88, verses 8–16:

﴿In a lofty Garden﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: The Garden is higher than the Fire, and therefore it is called "lofty." This is the view of al-Dahhak.

The second: The upper parts of the Garden and its chambers, because they are dwellings of height and elevation.

On this view, concerning their elevation within it, there are two views:

The first: That they may enjoy the height and elevation.

The second: That they may behold the blessings Allah has prepared for them within it.

﴿Wherein they will hear no idle talk﴾. Al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: that is, they will not hear in it any word of idle talk (laghw). Concerning what is meant by it there are seven sayings:

The first: It means falsehood. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: Sin. This is said by Qatadah.

The third: It is insult. This is said by Mujahid.

The fourth: Vanity. This is said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The fifth: Disobedience. This is said by al-Hasan.

The sixth: Oaths, so that in the Garden no one will hear an oath, whether by the righteous or the wicked. This is said by al-Kalbi.(p-261)

The seventh: No word in their speech will be left without purpose, because the people of the Garden speak only with wisdom and with praise of Allah for what He has provided them. This is said by al-Farra'.

﴿Therein are raised couches﴾. Al-Surur is the plural of sarir (couch), and it is derived from al-surur (joy). Concerning describing them as "raised," there are three aspects:

The first: Because some of them are raised above others.

The second: They are raised in their own estimation because of their dignity and their love for them. This is said by al-Farra'.

The third: That their place is raised because of their height and loftiness.

On this view, concerning describing them with loftiness and elevation, there are two views:

The first: That its people may enjoy its elevation. This is said by Ibn Shajarah.

The second: That by their elevation they may behold the dominion they have been given and the blessings they have been granted. This is said by Ibn 'Isa.

As for His saying ﴿and cups set in place﴾, al-akwab are the vessels, and the discussion of their interpretation has already passed.

Concerning His saying ﴿set in place﴾ there are two views:

The first: That they are in their hands for the enjoyment of looking at them, because they are of gold and silver.

The second: That is, that they are kept in continuous use, for the continuity of their drinking from them. This is said by al-Mufaddal.

﴿and cushions arranged﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: The pillows, whose singular is numruqah. This is said by Qatadah.

The second: The cushions for leaning on (al-marafiq). This is said by Ibn Abi Talhah, and the poet said:

"And a gazelle with large dark eyes, beloved, whose carpets are spread out and whose cushions [are arranged]."

﴿and carpets spread out﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: They are the fine rugs. This is said by Ibn 'Isa.

The second: They are the embroidered coverings. This is said by al-Kalbi and al-Farra'.

Concerning "spread out" (al-mabthuthah) there are four views:

The first: Stretched out. This is said by Qatadah.

The second: Some of them above others. This is said by 'Ikrimah.(p-262)

The third: Numerous. This is said by al-Farra'.

The fourth: Scattered about. This is said by Ibn Qutaybah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 88, verse 17–26:

﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ and the verses that follow. In his mention of these there are three aspects:

The first: that they may draw inference from the signs in them concerning the power of God the Exalted and His oneness.

The second: that they may know, through His power over these things, that He is able to resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The third: that when God the Exalted described to them what is in Paradise, the people of misguidance marvelled at it, so He mentioned to them these things together with their wondrousness, so that their astonishment would be removed. This was said by Qatada.

Regarding "al-Ibil" (the camels) here there are two views:

The first, which is the more apparent and the more well-known: that it refers to camels among the livestock (ni'am).

The second: that it refers to the clouds. If the intended meaning is the clouds, then it is because of the signs in them that indicate the power of God and the general benefits for all His creation.

If the intended meaning is the livestock, then the camel gathers more benefits than the rest of the animals, because its kinds are four: a milch animal (halubah), a riding animal (rakubah), an animal for eating (akulah), and a burden-carrying animal (humulah). The camel combines these four qualities, so the blessing through it is more general and the manifestation of power in it is more complete.

Then God the Exalted said after that: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder﴾. In it there are two views:

The first: "You are only a preacher."

The second: He reminded them of the blessings so that they would fear the punishments.(p-263)

﴿You are not over them a controller﴾. In it there are three sayings. The first: "You are not over them a dominator." This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: "a tyrant." This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The third: "a lord." This was said by al-Hasan. The meaning of the speech "you are not over them a controller" is that you cannot compel them to faith.

Then He said: ﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾. So you have no reminder for him, because he does not accept your reminder. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: "Except one who turns away and disbelieves, then leave him to God the Exalted." This was before fighting; then he was commanded to fight them. This was said by al-Hasan.

Regarding ﴿turns away and disbelieves﴾ there are two views:

The first: he turned away from the truth and disbelieved in the blessing.

The second: he turned away from the Messenger and disbelieved in God the Exalted. This was said by al-Dahhak.

﴿Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾: meaning Hell.

It may also mean abiding in it, for by its continuity it becomes greater than what is temporary.

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾: that is, their place of return.

﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾: meaning their recompense for their deeds, so that this combines promise and warning: reward for obedience and punishment for sins.
